title: HoardMQ configuration
description: Canonical configuration document for the HoardMQ broker, format version 1.

modules.description: Module configuration, nested under the module identifier.

sinkKafka.description: The Kafka forwarder: every publish this node accepts on a topic a route matches is produced to the route's Kafka topic. MQTT to Kafka only.

clientId.description: The Kafka client identifier. Default hoardmq-<node name>, or hoardmq without one.

tls.description: TLS to the brokers; the server certificate is always verified.

caFile.description: PEM CA certificates; default the system pool.

certFile.description: PEM client certificate; give keyFile too.

keyFile.description: PEM client key; give certFile too.

serverName.description: The name the server certificate must carry, when not the broker's host.

passwordFile.description: A file holding the password; one trailing newline is ignored. The password is never logged.

routes.description: Where messages go. A message is produced once to each distinct Kafka topic among the routes it matches; for a topic named twice, the first matching route decides.

filter.description: An MQTT topic filter, not a shared one.

topic.description: The Kafka topic: 1 to 249 of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-'.

key.description: The record key: the MQTT topic (default), the publisher's client identifier, the user property keyProperty names, or none.

keyProperty.description: The user property whose value is the key, with key userProperty.

namespace.description: The namespace whose messages the route matches. Default the node's default namespace.

metadata.description: Write the mqtt.* headers (topic, QoS, source, client identifier and the MQTT 5 properties that are set). Default true.

userProperties.description: Write each MQTT 5 user property as a header, in order. Default true.

acks.description: all (default; the idempotent producer) or leader.

lingerMs.description: How long a batch waits for more records. Default 5.

buffer.description: The in-memory buffer between accepted publishes and Kafka. A node that crashes loses what it holds.

whenFull.description: While the buffer is full: refuse (default) answers a client's matching QoS 1 or 2 publish with Quota Exceeded (0x97), or closes a 3.1.1 connection; drop accepts it and counts its forward dropped. QoS 0 forwards are dropped and counted under both.

waitMs.description: How long an admitted QoS 1 or 2 publish waits for room under refuse before its forward is counted overflow. Default 1000.

flushTimeoutMs.description: How long the forwarder flushes at stop; what remains is counted shutdown. Default 5000.

name.description: Node name within the cluster. Empty means undecided; a later component chooses.

dataDir.description: Directory holding this node's logs and checkpoints.

walSync.description: When log records are fsynced: before every QoS 1 and 2 acknowledgement (commit, the default) or on an interval (relaxed).

walSyncIntervalMs.description: Sync interval in milliseconds under the relaxed policy.

walGroupMaxDelayMs.description: Under the commit policy, how long a sync may hold to let concurrent callers share one fsync (group commit). 0, the default, never holds: only callers arriving while an fsync is in flight are grouped, which under load is all of them.

walGroupMaxSize.description: Fires a held group early once this many callers have joined; only matters when walGroupMaxDelayMs is non-zero. Default 256.

sessionShards.description: How many slices the session map is split into, rounded up to a power of two. One lock for the whole map made every connect, disconnect and inbound packet queue behind every other. Default 64.

storeAdmission.description: How many connects and disconnects may be inside the store's write path at once. Before the session map was sharded its single lock bounded this at one as a side effect; removing that bound entirely was measured catastrophic at 100,000 clients. 0 is unbounded. Default 64.

walSegmentBytes.description: Size at which a log segment rolls.

address.description: host:port to bind; the host may be empty.

path.description: HTTP path for ws and wss listeners. Default /mqtt.

maxConnections.description: Connections accepted at once on this listener; 0 means unlimited.

maxHandshakes.description: Connections accepted but not yet answered with a CONNACK; at the bound the listener pauses accepting and the kernel backlog absorbs the rest (pause-accept). 0 means the default, 512.

connectRate.description: CONNECTs a second this listener admits; one over it is refused before any credential is examined (0x9F at MQTT 5.0, closed at 3.1.1 and 3.1). 0, the default, is unlimited.

connectBurst.description: How many CONNECTs the listener admits at once before connectRate paces them. 0, the default, is twice connectRate. Needs connectRate.

cluster.description: Settings that must agree across nodes, and this node's place in the cluster transport.

listen.description: Address of the peer listener. Required when peers are configured.

peers.description: The other nodes of the cluster.

heartbeatMisses.description: Consecutive missed intervals before a peer is down.

maxFrameBytes.description: Largest frame accepted on the transport.

advertise.description: Client-facing address other nodes may hand out in a Server Reference.

drain.description: Graceful leave: clients are redirected at a bounded rate, the node's leases are handed to a live node, and the drain waits for its sessions to be confirmed held there.

ratePerSecond.description: The least number of clients a drain disconnects per second; it goes faster where that is what disconnects them all by timeoutMs less leases.takeoverTimeoutMs (or less half timeoutMs, if that is smaller).

timeoutMs.description: How long a drain waits for redirected clients to be taken over before handing the remaining leases off.

confirmTimeoutMs.description: How long a drain waits, after handing its leases off, for every session it held to be confirmed held by its receiver; sessions still unconfirmed then are counted and logged.

onSignal.description: Drain on SIGTERM before exiting, for setups without a preStop hook (bare containers, systemd). SIGINT and a second SIGTERM still shut down immediately.

holdExitMs.description: After a drain that no signal started completes, how long the process stays up waiting for SIGINT or SIGTERM before it exits; the signal ends the wait at once. For a Kubernetes preStop hook that waits on the drain: the hook reads the completion and exits before the process does. 0 exits as the drain completes.

stableMs.description: How long the topology (members, shard map, alive set) must be unchanged before the node reports ready; 0 disables the condition.

ackTimeoutMs.description: How long a QoS 1 or 2 acknowledgement waits for the followers to hold the message, and how long a takeover or adoption waits for a replica of a session.

syncMs.description: Interval of the full route-table exchange with every peer.

ttlMs.description: How long a lease stays valid without its owner renewing.

takeoverTimeoutMs.description: How long a lease decision or a state pull may take.

bootstrap.description: Whether this node may bootstrap a new group when no peer answers; absent means the lowest-named node may.

discovery.description: Where the peer set comes from.

dnsDiscovery.description: A StatefulSet's headless Service: peers are <name>-<i>.<service>:<port> for every ordinal below replicas.

clusterAuth.description: How peers authenticate each other. mtls uses certificates from the cluster CA; secret proves a shared secret with an HMAC and does not encrypt.

maxKeepAlive.description: Upper bound on a client's keep alive in seconds; 0 accepts the client's value.

connectTimeout.description: Seconds allowed from accept to CONNECT.

queueDrop.description: Which message a full session queue drops: the oldest queued or the newest arriving.

connectRate.description: CONNECTs a second this node admits across every listener; one over it is refused before any credential is examined. 0, the default, is unlimited.

connectBurst.description: How many CONNECTs the node admits at once before connectRate paces them. 0, the default, is twice connectRate. Needs connectRate.

maxSessionExpiry.description: Cap on the Session Expiry Interval in seconds; 0 means no cap.

clientMessageRate.description: PUBLISH packets a second each client may send; one over it is read later, not refused (the broker stops reading the socket until the rate allows). 0, the default, is unlimited.

clientMessageBurst.description: How many PUBLISH packets a client may send at once before clientMessageRate paces it. 0 is twice the rate. Needs clientMessageRate.

clientByteRate.description: PUBLISH topic and payload bytes a second each client may send, paced as clientMessageRate is. 0, the default, is unlimited.

clientByteBurst.description: How many bytes a client may send at once before clientByteRate paces it. 0 is twice the rate. Needs clientByteRate.

overload.description: The limits the node's stress level is measured against: each indicator's fraction of its limit sets a level (under 0.6 is 0, under 0.8 is 1, under 0.95 is 2, else 3) and the highest is the node's. 0 leaves an indicator out.

queuedMessages.description: Messages queued across this node's sessions. Default 1000000.

replicationLag.description: Replication frames sent to peers and not yet acknowledged, summed over the peers. Default 400000.

memoryBytes.description: The live heap's limit. 0, the default, uses the process's GOMEMLIMIT when one is set and otherwise leaves memory out.

flapping.description: A client whose established connections end abnormally on its side (the network drops, the keep-alive expires, the client breaks the protocol) maxCount times within windowSeconds on one node is banned by client identifier for banSeconds. A client DISCONNECT, and any end or refusal the broker chose, is never counted.

observability.description: The metrics, liveness and readiness listener, the audit log and trace recordings.

address.description: host:port for /metrics, /healthz and /readyz; empty (the default) serves nothing. A non-loopback host requires allowRemote.

queue.description: Events held for the audit writer; a refused connect is dropped and counted when the queue is full, every other event waits for space.

admin.description: The admin REST API: its own listener, off unless address is set. Every request is authenticated by a bearer token or a client certificate and authorized by the scopes of the identity it maps to.

address.description: host:port of the admin listener; empty (the default) binds nothing. A non-loopback host requires tls.

roles.description: Named scope sets that tokens, certificates and identity-provider groups are granted by name.

tokens.description: Bearer-token identities. The token is the trimmed content of tokenFile, at least 16 bytes; the document names the file, never the token.

certificates.description: Client-certificate identities, by the common name of a certificate tls.clientCAFile verifies.

maxBodyBytes.description: Largest request body accepted; larger bodies are refused with 413. Default 1048576.

adminToken.description: Holds the union of its scopes and its roles' scopes; at least one scope or role.

name.description: The identity's name; audit records name it as token:<name>.

adminCertificate.description: Holds the union of its scopes and its roles' scopes; at least one scope or role.

adminOIDC.description: Accepts ID tokens an OpenID Connect provider issued (hoardmq login obtains one) as bearer credentials, verified against the issuer's published keys; the identity's groups map to roles, and an identity no mapping grants a role is refused.

issuer.description: The provider's issuer URL, exactly as its ID tokens carry it: https, or http on a loopback host.

clientIds.description: Client identifiers whose ID tokens are accepted: a token's aud must name one.

usernameClaim.description: The claim naming the identity; audit records name it as oidc:<value>. Default sub.

groupsClaim.description: The claim listing the identity's groups. Default groups.

caFile.description: PEM certificates to verify the provider's TLS instead of the system roots.

clockSkewSeconds.description: Allowed disagreement between this node's clock and the provider's on exp, iat and nbf. Default 60.

maxTokenLifetimeSeconds.description: The longest exp - iat accepted, whatever the provider issues. Default 86400.

adminScope.description: read is every :read scope; admin is every scope.

hooks.description: How modules are called: the timeout and fallback of every hook call, and the module order.

order.description: Module identifiers called first, in this order, in every hook family, both authentication chains (certificate authenticators still before the rest) and the lifecycle (stop reversed); every other module follows in identifier order. Read at start: a change applies at the next restart.

timeoutMs.description: Milliseconds a hook may run before the fallback applies; 0 calls hooks inline with no deadline.

fallback.description: What a timed-out or panicking hook counts as.

anonymous.description: Accept connections that present no credentials when no authenticator decides. Default false.

decisionTtlSeconds.description: How long an authenticator's allow is held before it is made again without the client; a session whose credential no longer passes is ended. A token's own expiry, when sooner, is used instead. Default 3600.

argon2MemoryBytes.description: The memory this node's Argon2id password verifications may hold at once; a verification waits for its share, and a hash that needs more than all of it is refused. Default 268435456 (four at the default cost of 64 MiB).

cache.description: The node's cache of password verifications, so a reconnecting client is not made to derive its key again. An entry is a keyed MAC of the stored credential and the password with an expiry, never the password or a derived key; only a match is kept.

ttlSeconds.description: How long a verification is kept. 0 turns the cache off. Default 60.

maxEntries.description: Verifications kept at most; when full, a new one is not kept. Default 100000.

mqtt.description: MQTT 5.0 capabilities advertised in CONNACK. Every capability is on by default; switching one off is the operator's decision, not the product's.

sharedSubscriptionStrategy.description: How a shared subscription group picks the member that receives each message.
